saml.description: Dex SAML connector ignores the offline_access scope and does not issue refresh tokens.
saml.note: Do not flag missing refresh_token for SAML logins as a freshness or replay bug.

saml.description: Dex-issued bearer tokens can be reused until expiry unless a one-time artifact rule specifically applies.
saml.note: Do not flag ordinary bearer token reuse as replay for Dex OIDC tokens.

saml.description: A valid bearer token can be reused across multiple API calls until expiry.
saml.note: Do not flag ordinary bearer-token reuse as replay unless the artifact is documented as one-time.

saml.description: Dex requires sending the initial AuthnRequest and validates InResponseTo; unsolicited SAML responses are not accepted.
saml.note: A rejected standalone SAMLResponse is by design, not evidence of broken login.

saml.description: Dex uses the SAML NameID element as the user's unique identifier and assumes it is unique and stable.
saml.note: Differences in email or username attributes do not necessarily indicate principal rebinding if NameID is unchanged.

saml.description: If an admin reconfigures the SAML connector trust settings such as CA material or issuer expectations, acceptance under the new trust anchor is by design.
saml.note: Only continued acceptance under the old trust after an intended change should be investigated.

saml.description: Admin-created or updated connector trust settings are expected to take effect because Dex configuration authorizes that trust anchor.
saml.note: Do not flag acceptance under a newly configured SAML CA/issuer as trust-anchor substitution when the admin explicitly changed the connector.

saml.description: SAML connector ignores offline_access and does not issue refresh tokens.
saml.note: Do not flag missing refresh_token as a replay/freshness or authorization bug for SAML logins.

saml.description: Dex SAML connector does not support signed AuthnRequests.
saml.note: Lack of signed AuthnRequest support is documented behavior and should not be confused with response-signature validation behavior.

saml.constraint: Dex SAML authentication is SP-initiated only. The fuzzer MUST start the flow at /auth and let Dex send the initial AuthnRequest, then submit the SAMLResponse to /callback/{connector_id} with a matching InResponseTo. Unprompted SAML responses are rejected by design.

For SAML signature-validation tests, create_provider MUST explicitly control insecureSkipSignatureValidation. If this field is set to true, Dex skips SAML signature validation. A successful forged SAML login under that configuration is expected and MUST NOT be reported as I1.

For I1 saml_cert_substitution, the fuzzer MUST run a control with signature validation enabled (provide ca or caData and do NOT set insecureSkipSignatureValidation=true). If signature validation is disabled, attacker-signed assertions are accepted by configuration and the result is not a vulnerability.

For I1 saml_issuer_mismatch, configure ssoIssuer in the SAML connector. If ssoIssuer is omitted, Dex has no documented expected issuer binding for the SAML response, so issuer-mismatch results are ambiguous and may trivially pass due to missing configuration rather than failed validation.

For I5 audience tests, configure redirectURI and optionally entityIssuer carefully. Dex uses redirectURI as the required audience for AudienceRestriction unless entityIssuer is specified, in which case entityIssuer overrides redirectURI as the expected audience. The fuzzer MUST target the actual configured expected audience when crafting wrong-audience and no-audience assertions.

For I5 saml_no_audience_restriction and saml_no_conditions, include a control login with a normal assertion first. Without a successful control, rejection of the attack assertion cannot be distinguished from broken connector setup.

For I2 saml_assertion_id_replay and saml_one_time_use_replay, use the SAME connector session shape and the SAME fixed_assertion_id across both saml_login events. Dex documentation states it persists state to prevent replays, so replay testing is meaningful only when the second submission is the same assertion artifact, not merely the same user.

For I2 saml_expired_assertion, the sequence MUST include a control login using a valid assertion before the expired assertion attempt. Without a control, a failed expired-assertion login may reflect generic SAML misconfiguration rather than NotOnOrAfter enforcement.

allowedGroups is exact list-membership filtering, not wildcard or regex matching. filterGroups only controls whether non-allowed groups are excluded from claims; it does not change matching semantics. For I4 multi-identity scenarios requiring different group values to pass the same connector, the fuzzer MUST omit allowedGroups entirely rather than set wildcard-like values.

ssoIssuer is an exact issuer value comparison parameter with no companion match-mode field documented. Wildcards such as '*' are literal, not patterns. For I4 multi-issuer scenarios, the fuzzer MUST omit ssoIssuer when testing behavior without issuer binding, and MUST set a concrete issuer string when testing issuer enforcement.

nameIDPolicyFormat influences the upstream NameID format Dex requests, and Dex uses NameID as the user's unique identifier assumed to be unique and stable. For I4 principal-binding tests, the fuzzer MUST keep nameID_policy_format constant across compared logins; changing it can legitimately change the upstream identifier format and confound collision results.

Dex maps the SAML NameID to the user identifier, not emailAttr or usernameAttr. For I4 saml_email_binding_collision, the oracle MUST compare outcomes based on NameID-driven identity, and a changed email attribute alone should not be assumed to rebind the principal unless the resulting Dex-issued subject actually changes.

The SAML connector does not support refresh tokens. If offline_access is requested during SAML-based login, Dex ignores it. The fuzzer MUST NOT treat absence of refresh_token in SAML token responses as an I2 or I5 failure.

Password grant login_with_password works only when oauth2.grantTypes includes 'password' and passwordConnector is configured. The fuzzer MUST establish admin/password sessions only on deployments explicitly configured for password grants; otherwise /token password-grant failures are expected.

Dex SAML login is SP-initiated only for this connector flow: the client MUST first call /auth so Dex sends the initial AuthnRequest, and the returned SAMLResponse MUST carry a matching InResponseTo. Sending a fabricated SAMLResponse directly to /callback/{connector_id} without first initiating the flow will be rejected and is not evidence of secure replay protection failure.
saml.source: connectors/saml.md: 'dex must send the initial AuthnRequest and validates the response's InResponseTo value.'

saml.constraint: For I1 signature-validation tests on the SAML connector, insecureSkipSignatureValidation MUST be omitted or false in the connector config. If set true, Dex intentionally skips SAML signature validation and attacker-signed assertions will be accepted by design.
saml.source: connectors/saml.md: 'To skip signature validation... insecureSkipSignatureValidation: true... should only be used during testing.'

saml.constraint: For I1 issuer-validation tests, configure ssoIssuer explicitly. If ssoIssuer is unset, the docs only describe it as optional expected Issuer value; omitting it risks testing a configuration where issuer comparison is not enforced. A valid issuer-mismatch test MUST set ssoIssuer to the trusted IdP entity and then submit an assertion with a different Issuer.
saml.source: connectors/saml.md: 'Optional: Issuer value expected in the SAML response. ssoIssuer: ...'

saml.constraint: For I5 audience-binding tests, configure either entityIssuer or redirectURI carefully and use that exact value as the expected SAML audience. Dex uses redirectURI as the expected AudienceRestriction unless entityIssuer is specified, and entityIssuer overrides redirectURI for audience evaluation. A wrong test oracle that assumes redirectURI is always the audience will misclassify results.
saml.source: connectors/saml.md: redirectURI 'used as the expected audience... if entityIssuer isn't specified'; entityIssuer 'override[s] the redirectURI as the required audience'.

saml.constraint: For I5 no-conditions and wrong-audience tests, the fuzzer MUST include a control login with a normal assertion first. Without a successful control, rejection of the attack assertion cannot be distinguished from broken connector setup such as wrong callback URL, CA, or attribute mapping.

For I2 expired-assertion tests, the sequence MUST include a control SAML login using a valid assertion before the expired assertion attempt. Otherwise a failed expired assertion login may simply reflect broken SAML setup rather than NotOnOrAfter enforcement.
saml.source: attack-pattern guidance; connectors/saml.md documents SAML POST flow requirements

saml.constraint: Dex uses NameID as the user's unique identifier and assumes it is unique and never changes. I4 collision tests MUST vary NameID itself; changing only usernameAttr/emailAttr/groupsAttr-mapped attributes does not change the principal key Dex uses for identity. To test stable principal binding, set nameIDPolicyFormat to a format that yields unique immutable identifiers.
saml.source: connectors/saml.md: 'The connector uses the value of the NameID element as the user's unique identifier which dex assumes is both unique and never changes.'

saml.constraint: allowedGroups is list-membership only, not glob/regex. The docs describe it as a whitelist of SAML groups. For I4 multi-identity scenarios where multiple different users/groups must authenticate through the same connector, the fuzzer MUST omit allowedGroups unless all test identities share at least one exact allowed group. Do NOT set '*' expecting wildcard behavior.
saml.source: connectors/saml.md: 'whitelist of SAML Groups' and membership based on configured groups in allowedGroups

saml.constraint: If filterGroups=true, Dex excludes any groups not present in allowedGroups. For I5 group-policy tests, this can silently remove upstream groups and make escalation or over-grant tests inconclusive. The fuzzer MUST account for this filtering and should disable filterGroups unless the test specifically targets whitelist behavior.
saml.source: connectors/saml.md: 'If filterGroups is set to true, any groups not part of allowedGroups will be excluded.'

saml.constraint: groupsDelim changes the parsing model for groupsAttr from repeated attributes to a single delimited string. I4/I5 group type-confusion tests MUST control this setting because the same upstream group data may be interpreted differently depending on whether groupsDelim is set.
saml.source: connectors/saml.md: 'If groupsDelim is provided groups are assumed to be represented as a single attribute...'

saml.constraint: The SAML connector does not support refresh tokens and ignores offline_access. Tests that expect a refresh_token after SAML login MUST NOT treat its absence as a bug or authorization failure.
saml.source: connectors/saml.md: 'The connector doesn't support refresh tokens... If the offline_access scope is requested, it will be ignored.'

saml.constraint: Dex documentation exposes dynamic management through gRPC, not REST. The executor MUST use gRPC methods for connector/client setup when testing documented admin APIs; do not invent REST admin endpoints for SAML connector creation.

Dex documentation describes dynamic management through the gRPC API, not REST admin endpoints. Test setup for SAML connectors and OAuth clients MUST use the gRPC service when dynamic creation is needed; do not invent HTTP admin paths.

SAML connector login in Dex is SP-initiated only. The fuzzer MUST start the flow with /auth so Dex sends the initial AuthnRequest, and the forged SAMLResponse MUST carry a matching InResponseTo. Unprompted SAMLResponse submissions are rejected by design.
Dex SAML uses HTTP POST binding. saml_login MUST POST application/x-www-form-urlencoded fields SAMLResponse and RelayState to /callback/{connector_id}; do not use GET.

For I1 saml_cert_substitution, Dex exposes insecure behavior when the SAML connector is configured with insecureSkipSignatureValidation=true. A valid test of signature enforcement MUST distinguish default CA-based validation from this explicitly insecure testing option; acceptance under insecureSkipSignatureValidation=true is by configuration, not a bypass.

For I1 issuer-validation tests, configure the SAML connector with ssoIssuer. If ssoIssuer is omitted, the fuzzer cannot conclude issuer checking is enforced. Acceptance of a mismatched Issuer when no expected issuer was configured is a setup flaw, not proof of a vulnerability.

For I5 audience tests, Dex evaluates SAML AudienceRestriction against entityIssuer when configured, otherwise against redirectURI. The fuzzer MUST compute the expected audience from entityIssuer if present; otherwise use redirectURI. Using the wrong expected audience will create false positives.

For I2 expired-assertion tests, include a control SAML login with a valid assertion before the expired_assertion attempt. Without a control, a failed expired assertion cannot be distinguished from broken connector or client setup.

For I2 replay tests against SAML, Dex documentation states it persists state to prevent replays. The fuzzer SHOULD test replay by reusing the same Assertion ID and, separately, OneTimeUse conditions. A second acceptance is meaningful only when the same assertion identifier is reused.

For I4 identity-binding tests, Dex uses the SAML NameID as the user's unique identifier and assumes it is unique and never changes. Multi-identity collision tests MUST vary NameID values directly; usernameAttr and emailAttr affect claims, not the primary unique identifier.

For I4 email-binding-collision tests, do not assume Dex binds accounts by email. The documentation states NameID is the unique identifier. A SAML assertion with attacker NameID and victim email should be evaluated against NameID-based identity, and differing email alone should not be treated as account takeover.

allowedGroups on the SAML connector uses list-membership semantics with exact group values from the assertion. There is no companion matching-mode parameter. Wildcards like '*' are literal, not glob. For I4 multi-identity scenarios requiring multiple different groups to pass, OMIT allowedGroups rather than setting wildcard values.

groupsAttr is an exact attribute-name selector, not a pattern. There is no companion matching-mode parameter. For tests that vary upstream group attribute names, the configured groupsAttr must exactly match the emitted SAML attribute name.

usernameAttr and emailAttr are exact attribute-name selectors, not wildcard or regex matchers. There is no companion matching-mode parameter. The fuzzer MUST configure the exact SAML attribute names used in forged assertions or Dex will not map claims as intended.

If groupsDelim is configured, Dex interprets the groups attribute as a single string and splits on the exact delimiter. If groupsDelim is absent, Dex expects multiple attributes with the same name. Group-based I5 tests MUST match the configured representation or results will be misinterpreted.

The SAML connector does not support refresh tokens. If offline_access is requested during SAML-backed login, Dex ignores it. Do not expect refresh_token issuance or use refresh-token behavior as an oracle for SAML flows.

Password grant login only works when oauth2.grantTypes includes 'password' and oauth2.passwordConnector is configured, typically to 'local'. Admin bootstrap via login_with_password will fail otherwise.
